newsitem.title: USA: Florida Power plant added to NRC watchlist.
newsitem.headline: Florida Power plant added to NRC watchlist.

text.p: Florida Power Corp said Wednesday its Crystal River 3 plant was added to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) watchlist of nuclear power plants.
The 860 megawatt (MW) unit, in Red Level, Fla., has been shut for an extended maintenance outage since Sept 2, 1996.
The watchlist, issued semi-annually, identifies plants the NRC believes need sharpened regulatory attention until a period of improved performance has been demonstrated.
"The NRC cited the nuclear plant's 1996 decline in overall performance as the primary reason for putting the plant on the list," the company said.
Florida Power said the main reason for extending the outage involves a loading problem with one of the plant's two emergency diesel generators that are part of the emergency core cooling system.
The generators would provide backup power if there were a loss of off-site power to the plant.

"The company is currently evaluating options to address the generator issue. Assuming it can be successfully resolved by the fourth quarter of 1997, the plant is expected to return to service by year-end," the company said in a statement.

The Crystal River plant, Florida Power Corp's only nuclear generating station, was given a category 2 designation on the watchlist, which means it can continue to operate but under close monitoring by the NRC.

In late 1996, the company launched a program to address the NRC's performance concerns. Areas cited for improvement included management oversight, engineering performance, operator performance, and regulatory compliance.
"We are confident that we have a comprehensive plan that will help return the unit to top performance," said Joe Richardson, president and chief operating officer.

Florida Power Corp, the state's second-largest electric utility, is the principal subsidiary of St. Petersburg-based Florida Progress Corp and serves 1.3 million customers in central and northern Florida.
